newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes firm, riding high on strong dlr.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes firm, riding high on strong dlr.

text.p: German share prices continued to rally on Monday, albeit at a slower pace than last week, as export-led stocks like carmakers were boosted by the dollar which hit a seven-and-a-half year high against the mark.
The DAX index, which reflects dealing in 30 blue-chip shares, closed floor trading up 1.24 percent at 4,371.16, just below the day's high of 4,379.88.
Dealers said the market had calmed down from last week's heady record-setting spree but predicted further gains were in store despite a prospect for some consolidation.
The U.S. dollar's stubborn strength is one of the main factors powering the German share index higher, as it is seen to help a host of export-driven companies.
"....we see the long-term upward trend on the bourse as remaining stable," analysts at Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG wrote in a note to investors.
"Signs of interim technical corrections have strengthened recently but the corrections should be limited. Weak days therefore continue to be suited to appropriate portfolio increases."
Corporate earnings are rising amid low-inflation growth and historically low interest rates, while Germany's savers appear finally to have acknowledged equities as a viable investment, analysts said.

Chemical, engineering and carmaking stocks were among the favourites on Monday, helped by the dollar which was trading at 1.8440 marks in early afternoon European trade. The U.S. unit earlier hit 1.8470 marks, its highest level in seven-and-a-half years.

Electrical giant Siemens AG rose more than six percent to a record high of 130.50 marks in floor trade, gaining from positive analysts' assessments in the wake of nine-month results published least week. The shares closed at 130 marks.

Sportswear maker Puma also fared very well rising over six percent to close floor trade at 54.90 marks on market talk a foreign retailer might be extending its feelers toward buying up the German company. There was no official comment on the matter available immediately however.
